title: Epistemic stewardship discovery chain
status: retrospective reconstruction from conversation and repository history
principles: Contribution provenance is separate from epistemic authority.
Epistemic authority should not exceed defensibility.
Origin deserves credit. Authority requires warrant.
Low authority should trigger handoff, not erasure.

actors.label: OpenAI ChatGPT
actors.model_note: GPT-5.6 Sol for the session in which this graph was recorded; earlier contributions should be understood as ChatGPT contributions unless model-specific evidence is preserved.

nodes.label: Cognitive abundance
nodes.summary: Machine cognition sharply lowers the cost of producing candidate arguments, code, hypotheses and other intellectual artefacts.

contributions.note: Developed the broader Agalmic Research programme around abundance of machine cognition and knowledge production.
Helped organize the abundance framing into research tracks and draft language.

nodes.label: Authorial Capacity Gap
nodes.summary: Artefact sophistication can increase faster than the human curator's ability to understand and defend it.

contributions.note: Raised the problem through concern about Dunning–Kruger, human author/curator capacity and personal inability to defend machine-assisted work commensurate with its apparent quality.
Named and developed the Authorial Capacity Constraint and distinguished artefact quality from curator comprehension and defensibility.

nodes.label: Principle of Defensible Stewardship
nodes.summary: Epistemic authority should not exceed defensibility.

contributions.note: Motivated the principle through the authorial-capacity concern and chose to make it the governing principle and first-paper focus.
Proposed the compact formulation 'Epistemic authority should not exceed defensibility' and the label Principle of Defensible Stewardship.

nodes.label: The Authorial Capacity Constraint
nodes.summary: Working Paper 001 on authorship, defensibility and epistemic stewardship under cognitive abundance.

contributions.note: Introduced the central concern, supplied key future directions, chose transparency as the first-paper strategy and authorised publication.
Developed terminology and structure, drafted substantial prose, introduced distinctions, generated counterarguments and helped shape the research programme.

nodes.label: Human-Scale Epistemic Horizon
nodes.summary: Frontier knowledge may eventually exceed the point at which any unaided human can personally comprehend and defend the best available results.

contributions.note: Raised the possibility that increasing machine capability could diminish epistemic authority on the human scale, connecting it to singularity thinking and suggesting mathematics as an early domain.
Named the Human-Scale Epistemic Horizon and framed it as a clearly marked deep-future conjecture rather than a prediction.

nodes.label: Principle of Separable Epistemic Roles
nodes.summary: Epistemic contribution and epistemic authority should be separable.

contributions.note: Introduced the larger problem of harnessing ideas from non-experts and explicitly proposed separating initiator credentials from those with epistemic authority over a work.
Formulated the separable-roles principle and the compact phrase 'Origin deserves credit. Authority requires warrant.'

nodes.label: Epistemic handoff
nodes.summary: A structured transfer of candidate knowledge from an initiator toward actors who can frame, validate, verify, develop or realize it while preserving originator credit.

contributions.note: Supplied the practical pattern: 'It's my idea but I don't know if it's worth anything' should be followed by someone capable taking a look and helping make use of it.
Named the process epistemic handoff and developed the two-ledger and routing interpretation.

nodes.label: Epistemic Uptake Constraint
nodes.summary: As candidate knowledge becomes abundant, the capacity to notice, route, evaluate, validate, integrate and realize valuable contributions becomes scarce.

contributions.note: Motivated the need for society to harness valuable ideas from initiators who cannot themselves judge them.
Named and formulated the Epistemic Uptake Constraint as an instance of displaced scarcity.

nodes.label: Institutions for routing knowledge
nodes.summary: Knowledge systems need mechanisms for routing low-authority candidate ideas toward scarce expert attention, verification and realization while preventing appropriation, credential capture, flooding and filter monopoly.

contributions.note: Pushed the discussion from attribution toward the larger question of how useful knowledge can still be harnessed.
Expanded the institutional consequences, failure modes and possible epistemic supply-chain roles.

nodes.label: Epistemic Handoff: Contribution, Authority and Uptake Under Cognitive Abundance
nodes.summary: Draft paper developing separable contribution and authority, handoff, uptake scarcity and institutional routing.

contributions.note: Introduced the central separation between the idea initiator and those with epistemic authority and requested the website and paper programme be updated accordingly.
Named epistemic handoff and uptake, drafted the exploratory paper and developed failure modes and research questions.

nodes.label: The Defensibility Layer
nodes.summary: A proposed open infrastructure layer for recording human/machine contribution, verification and demonstrated defensibility in AI-assisted research.

contributions.note: Identified the IFP Launch Sequence opportunity and chose to pursue review of a practical proposal.
Proposed the Defensibility Layer as a concrete implementation direction and drafted/adversarially reviewed the pitch.

correction_policy: Attributions and edges may be corrected when better evidence appears. Corrections should be committed with an explanation rather than silently rewritten.
